Waterfront Views

Set on the northern tip of Siesta Key, Bay Horizon captures expansive views toward downtown Sarasota, the Ringling Bridge, and Bird Key.

The 9,300-square-foot residence is organized to support both daily living and large-scale entertainment. Generous indoor-outdoor connections extend the living experience, with over 5,700 square feet of covered terraces and an elevated infinity-edge pool that aligns with the main living level — reinforcing visual continuity with the water and skyline beyond.

On the Boards

Design to Reality

From Vision to Built

The journey from architectural rendering to completed home is where CMSA's process comes to life. Bay Horizon began as a series of carefully studied renderings — each one resolving the site's unique challenges and articulating the vision before a single foundation was poured.

Rendering

The framed arrival sequence — a defined entry wall, custom gate, and wraparound drive — was resolved in design long before construction began, ensuring the architecture revealed itself progressively as intended.

View Full Project
Beyond the Boards

The Details

The Process

Every detail was an opportunity — from a sculptural floating stair to gallery walls designed around an art collection decades in the making.

Bay Horizon incorporates features tailored precisely to the client's lifestyle: gallery-like spaces for an extensive art collection, a glass elevator with a custom underwater mural, and a sculptural floating stair that anchors the home's vertical circulation as an architectural statement. Garage doors are fully integrated into the façade with flush detailing and continuous cladding, maintaining the home's clean modern expression.

Spaces & Light

Public spaces and the owner's suite occupy the main level, while guest accommodations and a secondary gathering space are positioned above. Every room is oriented to the water — maximizing natural light and reinforcing the home's deep connection to its coastal setting. Material selection focused on durability and warmth: a composite wood-look cladding weathers the salt air while giving the home a refined, grounded presence.
